From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: EdgeGate private deploy — perf post-call & action items

Hi Rachel — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can scope the Private/VPC perf run properly. TL;DR: we want to verify tail latency and streaming resilience, confirm peering/VPN behavior, and validate concurrency/throughput at your expected peak.

Key perf targets discussed (please confirm these are the right goals):
- API tail latency: 95th < 150ms, 99th < 300ms for single-turn text gen (non-streaming)
- Streaming tail: end-to-end token stream latency (95th) < 250ms for 1KB token bursts
- Concurrency: support for 200 concurrent streaming sessions with <3% token-drop rate
- Throughput: sustained 800 req/s for 256-token average responses (burst capacity to 1.5k req/s)
- Internal app → inference node RTT budget: <30ms (to keep request-queueing low)

Network constraints we should validate:
- Peering/VPN path: you mentioned traffic will traverse a firewall with DPI (adds ~10–20ms). We need an exact test path (source IPs, egress NAT/inspection).
- Egress bandwidth: target baseline >= 1Gbps, with headroom for bursts (we can run throughput tests at 2Gbps if your link supports it).
- Preferred transport for streaming: HTTP/2 gRPC streaming or WebSocket? (we support gRPC and HTTP chunked streaming; WebRTC requires additional infra).

Attachments: I attached a simple network topo and a POC matrix with test phases (connectivity smoke, small-scale streaming, full-scale load).

Proposed next steps (dates tentative):
1) Your ops provides peering/VPN details + egress test IPs (by 2028-03-15) — action: Rachel
2) Redwood provides test harness repo & lightweight runbook (by 2028-03-16) — action: Ben/Karthik
3) Connectivity smoke test (small scale) — target window 2028-03-20
4) Full perf run (concurrency + streaming) — target window 2028-04-03

Questions for you:
- Can your firewall maintain TLS passthrough for the inference flows or will it terminate and re-encrypt?
- Any IP allowlist requirements on your side for outbound callbacks or monitoring beacons?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short ops call if that helps.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: EdgeGate private deploy — perf post-call & action items

Ben — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our infra team:
- Topology: our inference gateway sits behind a perimeter firewall (checkpoint cluster) that currently does TLS termination for inbound traffic and then re-establishes TLS to internal services. That termination adds ~12–18ms on average; with DPI rules it can spike higher.
- Bandwidth: our colo link is 10Gbps, but the firewall applies session inspection which limits single-flow TCP to ~2Gbps unless we tune flow tables. We can open a high-performance path for the test if Redwood provides a list of source IPs and ports.
- Streaming transport: our preferred approach is HTTP/2 (gRPC) since our front door already supports it. We also want to evaluate QUIC for streaming — if Redwood can provide a QUIC-enabled endpoint it's useful, otherwise gRPC is fine.

We can deliver the peering/VPN details and the block diagram by EOD Thu (2028-03-15). We'd like the smoke test the week of 3/20 and the full run in the following week (4/3 works). Also: we need to confirm data-at-rest controls for logs generated by the test harness (will Redwood redact tokens/requests?).

I'll loop in our infra alias ops@edgegate.io with the diagram.

—
Rachel Tan
Infrastructure Lead, EdgeGate Solutions
rachel.tan@edgegate.io

Thanks Rachel — that timing works. A couple of quick answers and clarifications: 
- TLS termination: Redwood's Private control plane can operate in two modes for this POC: TLS passthrough (end-to-end) or terminate at the customer edge and re-initiate to the inference cluster. For the cleanest latency numbers we recommend passthrough during the perf runs; if that isn't possible we will run both flows and compare.
- QUIC: our runtime has an experimental QUIC path for streaming; it's not default in Private pack installs but we can enable for the POC. We will highlight any differences vs HTTP/2 in the runbook.
- Data redaction: Redwood's test harness will redact prompt content by default for telemetry captured during the public POC; for private installs we will provide an option to keep telemetry internal to your VPC and to store logs to your KMS-backed bucket. We'll include explicit redaction settings in the runbook.

Action items (updated):
1) Rachel/EdgeGate: provide network diagram + egress/firewall details + allowlist by 2028-03-15 (you confirmed)
2) Redwood: publish test harness repo + runbook + QUIC toggle by 2028-03-16 — deliverable: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-edgegate-topology (stub)
3) Karthik: lead the smoke test orchestration on 2028-03-20 (small scale streaming + connectivity) — action: Karthik
4) Marissa: coordinate ops schedule and incident contact list for full run (target 2028-04-03) — action: Marissa

I'll also attach a lightweight runbook stub (redwood-runbook-stub.md) — it's a checklist for connectivity checks, ports, and a minimal load profile to run during the smoke test.

If you'd like, we can do a 30-minute ops call on Thu (3/15) once you hand over the diagram — say 10am PT?
